slot.brief: Circuit diagram of two-input gates (NAND/NOR/...) combined; determine the Boolean output for given inputs and name the equivalent gate.

stem: For the circuit shown in the figure, what is the output sequence for input pairs $(A,B)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)$, and which single gate is equivalent?

verdicts.working: All gates are NAND. Let P=¬(AB), Q=¬(AP), and R=¬(BP). Then Y=¬(QR)=A⊕B, giving (0,1,1,0).

working:
$P=(AB)'$, $Q=(AP)'$, $R=(BP)'$, $Y=(QR)'$
$AB=00,01,10,11\Rightarrow Y=0,1,1,0$
Equivalent gate: XOR.

Independent check: All gates are NAND. Let P=¬(AB), Q=¬(AP), and R=¬(BP). Then Y=¬(QR)=A⊕B, giving (0,1,1,0).

draft.stem: For the circuit shown in the figure, what is the output sequence for input pairs $(A,B)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)$, and which single gate is equivalent?

figure.description: Draw four two-input NAND gates, each represented by an AND-gate shape with a small output inversion bubble. Place G1 at the upper left, G2 and G3 in the middle with G2 above G3, and G4 at the right. Input A enters from the left and branches to one input of G1 and one input of G2. Input B enters from the left and branches to the other input of G1 and one input of G3. Label the output of G1 as P and branch this wire to the remaining inputs of G2 and G3. Label the output of G2 as Q and the output of G3 as R; connect Q and R to the two inputs of G4. Label the output of G4 as Y. Mark all wire junctions with dots; crossing wires without dots are not connected.

draft.distractor_notes:
A: treats the network as an AND gate.
C: treats the network as an OR gate.
D: gives the complement of XOR, confusing XOR with XNOR.
